EDGEFIX AI / SYNTHETIC TRAINING MATERIAL
Cooling and overheating
Overheating can result from blocked cooling passages, excessive ambient temperature, overload,
poor ventilation, unbalanced supply, or bearing friction. First review load and operating history and
compare temperature readings with the established baseline and site limits. With the equipment
safely isolated, inspect external cooling fins, fan cover, and air passages for dust or debris. Clean
only by an approved method that will not drive contamination into the motor. Confirm the fan and
shroud are intact and unobstructed.
Do not touch a hot housing to estimate temperature. Use a suitable calibrated instrument from a
safe position. If temperature continues to rise, trips recur, or the cause is uncertain, stop and refer
to a qualified electrical or mechanical technician.

EDGEFIX AI / SYNTHETIC TRAINING MATERIAL
Routine motor inspection
EdgeFix synthetic training document | Revision 1.0
Before work, identify the motor, driven load, operating duty, and recorded baseline. Inspect the
frame for impact, corrosion, loose guards, oil or water ingress, and blocked ventilation. Record
ambient temperature, load, sound, vibration, and bearing housing temperature at repeatable points.
Compare readings with the equipment record and site limits; this guide does not define universal
acceptance limits.
Preventive maintenance intervals must follow the site schedule and motor supplier requirements.
Keep a dated log of observations, measurements, corrective work, and parts fitted. A change from
the established baseline warrants investigation even when the motor still runs.

EDGEFIX AI / SYNTHETIC TRAINING MATERIAL
Lubrication and bearings
Bearing noise, rising housing temperature, or vibration may indicate lubrication problems,
contamination, misalignment, or wear. Record the bearing location and operating condition. Check
the maintenance record for lubricant type, quantity, and service date. Use only the specified
lubricant and approved service method; incompatible greases can damage bearings. Do not add
lubricant solely because a bearing is noisy.
Inspect for leakage, damaged seals, and contamination after isolation. A rough bearing, persistent
abnormal noise, or repeat temperature rise requires qualified assessment. Bearing replacement
and internal motor work are outside this guide.

Belt inspection and alignment
A belt drive can produce vibration, heat, and premature wear when tension or alignment is
incorrect. After safe shutdown and isolation, inspect belt surfaces for glazing, cracking, fraying,
contamination, and uneven wear. Check pulley grooves and mounting for visible damage. Use an
appropriate alignment tool and the equipment specification to assess pulley alignment. Use the
drive maker's specified tension method; do not estimate tension by hand.
Replace matched belt sets together where the drive design requires it. Refit guards before
operation. If alignment or tension cannot be verified to specification, refer the work to qualified
maintenance staff.

Belt heat and wear
A hot belt or uneven edge wear may be associated with misalignment, incorrect tension, damaged
pulleys, overload, or contamination. After isolation, inspect belt and pulley condition and verify
alignment and tension against the drive specification with suitable tools. Never adjust a moving
drive. If the specification is unavailable, do not guess; obtain the equipment data or qualified
support.

RECOMMENDED CHECKS: With the equipment safely isolated, inspect external cooling fins, fan cover, and air passages for dust or debris
Clean only by an approved method that will not drive contamination into the motor
Confirm the fan and shroud are intact and unobstructed
Inspect the frame for impact, corrosion, loose guards, oil or water ingress, and blocked ventilation
Keep a dated log of observations, measurements, corrective work, and parts fitted
SAFETY: Follow site-specific safety procedures and lockout/tagout requirements before physical inspection.
UNCERTAINTY: The image and retrieved passages do not establish the cause. Confirm observations using approved site methods.
